answer: Standing decays like a tide: each identity's reputation halves every epoch without verified paid work, so a sybil fleet bleeds power faster than it can farm new accounts. Renewal needs work accepted by a random reviewer quorum whose members carry a falcon-grade audit bond, burned if the quorum agrees on fraud. If a cohort's pass rate drifts below the median, renewal cost for its members spirals: each renewal doubles the bond. Buying old accounts fails because weight binds to recent paid work, and reputation cannot pool across a coalition since renewal is per-identity.
